A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure shorten the time from first symptom to treatment start for lung cancer patients, and by how many days?
Measure: Same-day chest X-ray report with immediate CT. A radiologist or reporting radiographer reads primary-care chest X-rays while the patient waits; if suspicious, CT is done the same day or within days and the referral is triggered by radiology.
effect_summary_en: A randomised trial in London (Thorax 2023) found that a median of 32 days passed from chest X-ray to lung cancer diagnosis when the X-ray was reported immediately, against 63 days with standard reporting, a 31-day saving.
supported_en: A randomised trial in Thorax (2023) found the median time from chest X-ray to diagnosis was 32 days with immediate reporting and 63 days with standard reporting (p=0.03), a 31-day saving.
not_supported_en: The trial included only 49 cancers in one London hospital, reported no confidence interval, and does not show the effect in a Finnish setting.
in_use_summary_en: No Tyks or Varha page read says that chest X-rays from health centres are reported while the patient waits, or that radiology starts a same-day CT or the referral; the Tyks pathway says the referral comes from primary care.
summary_en: Tyks's pages say lung cancer diagnosis is centralised at its lung clinic and that primary care writes the referral; they do not mention same-day X-ray reporting or radiology starting the CT. Tyks reports an average of 9 days from referral arrival to first contact in January–June 2025. A London randomised trial (Thorax 2023) found immediate reporting halved the time from chest X-ray to diagnosis, from 63 to 32 days.
unanswered_en: After three search rounds, no Varha or Tyks page was found that describes how fast health-centre chest X-rays are reported or how long it takes from X-ray to CT.
